Since its start as the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009, Waymo has focused on building the Waymo Driver—The World's Most Experienced Driver™—to improve access to mobility while saving thousands of lives now lost to traffic crashes. The Waymo Driver powers Waymo’s fully autonomous ride-hail service and can also be applied to a range of vehicle platforms and product use cases. The Waymo Driver has provided over ten million rider-only trips, enabled by its experience autonomously driving over 100 million miles on public roads and tens of billions in simulation across 15+ U.S. states.

 Hardware Engineering is an innovative and collaborative group of electrical, mechanical, reliability, software and vehicle engineers. We design, build, and perfect the products which are the eyes and ears of Waymo's autonomous driving technology, and integrate those products into vehicle platforms. We're seeking curious and talented teammates to keep us moving in the right direction.

 This role follows a hybrid work schedule and you will report to a Hardware Engineering Manager 

 You will: 

Lead all stages of project planning and development by owning SIPI (Signal Integrity/Power Integrity) for products and sub-systems

 Establish comprehensive SIPI guidelines and stack-up specifications through feasibility studies; collaborate with cross-functional teams to resolve SIPI challenges

 Audit layout routing and component placement for all interfaces to maximize SIPI performance

 Perform SIPI simulation for PCB, connectors, cabling and sign-off designs

 Measure and correlate with simulation models, enhancing model accuracy

 Research and integrate advanced SI/PI technologies to improve simulation efficiency, consistency, and precision

You have: 

Masters Degree in Electrical Engineering with 3+ years relevant working experience

 Ability to perform system level SIPI design, modeling and optimization with simulation softwares such as  HFSS, SIwave, PowerSI, ADS, HSPICE

 Familiarity with lab equipment such as oscilloscope, VNA, and TDR

 Demonstrated experience with simulation-to-measurement correlation

 Hands-on capability in lab environments to debug and resolve SI/PI-related issues

 Excellent communication skills with experience to collaborate with internal and external teams

We prefer: 

Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering with relevant experience

 Expertise in one or more of the following areas: SERDES, SoC Power Integrity (PI) with VR modeling, or LPDDRx interfaces

 Experience in root-cause analysis and debugging of real-world SI/PI hardware issues

 Streamlined SI/PI workflows through custom tool automation and scripting [Python/Tcl]

 Familiar with automotive-grade interfaces such as xGBase-T1, CAN/CAN-FD, LVDS, GMSL

 Experience with DoE simulation for high-volume production intended designs

 The system architecture team handles the onboard contract of the model with the system, including kinematics, interfaces and representations. Our team’s mission is to work across the stack, building the best setup for the model to drive. We tackle this through projects in data, modeling, metrics, and the overall planner system.

 In this role, you will report to a Technical Lead Manager.  

 You will: 

Tackle challenging real-world problems with ML and engineering solutions.

 Use state of the art techniques to design and build ML models, deploy them in the real world on production vehicles

 Design and build the necessary architectures, algorithms, pipelines and evaluation systems on Google's extensive data infrastructure

 Collaborate with researchers, product area owners and engineers to develop safe, smooth planning behavior for all road users & deliver product requirements.

You have: 

Bachelors in Computer Science, ML, Robotics, similar technical field of study, or equivalent practical experience

 Hands-on experience with modern deep learning libraries (eg: TensorFlow, JAX, Pytorch) 

 Proficient programming skills (eg: Python, C/C++)
